solutions.method: Integrate the force of an induced spherical dipole, including its demagnetizing response.
assumptions: B is the imposed coil induction at the initial ball centre, with the small ball absent. The coil current is maintained and the field is locally uniform over the ball.
The ball is a homogeneous isotropic linear paramagnet. Here chi is intrinsic material susceptibility defined by J=chi H_internal; spherical demagnetization gives chi_eff=chi/(1+chi/3).

Slow displacement means quasistatic mechanical work without a change of kinetic energy. The requested positive work is that of the external agent pulling the paramagnet out; magnetic-force work has the opposite sign.

steps.explanation: Self-consistency between the internal H and sphere demagnetizing field fixes its induced moment.
steps.math_latex: H_{\rm in}=H_0-J/3,\quad J=\chi H_{\rm in},\qquad p_m=\frac{V\chi}{\mu_0(1+\chi/3)}B=\frac{V\chi_{\rm eff}}{\mu_0}B.

steps.explanation: Integrate the position-dependent induced dipole force. The magnetic mechanical potential includes the induced-response factor one half.
The final field is negligible, so external extraction work is the increase of this potential.
steps.math_latex: \boxed{A_{\rm ext}=\frac{V\chi B^2}{2\mu_0(1+\chi/3)}};\qquad |\chi|\ll1:\quad A_{\rm ext}\simeq\frac{V\chi B^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad A_{\rm magnetic}=-A_{\rm ext}.

answers.label: External quasistatic extraction work for intrinsic material susceptibility
If supplied chi is already defined relative to external H0
answers.notes: Do not apply the demagnetizing factor a second time when susceptibility is defined against the imposed field.

checks: Work is positive for extracting a paramagnet from the field; it vanishes with initial B.
The integrated result is independent of the detailed path along the axis because the dipole-force potential depends only on local B².
The factor one half follows by integrating a moment proportional to B. Treating the final induced moment as constant would overcount the work.
limitations: Nonlinear susceptibility, hysteresis, a large ball or a coil field appreciably changed by the specimen requires additional constitutive/geometric information.
